source.title: ToolAlignBench: Investigating Alignment Conflicts in Tool-Calling Enabled LLMs
source.authors: Aryan Keluskar; Amrita Bhattacharjee; Huan Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study uses publicly available abliterated checkpoints to investigate tool-calling behaviors, but it does not measure refusal or the proposed residual-stream direction. Its reported outcomes are external contact and overall misalignment, not the refusal behavior named by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper describes abliteration as removing a refusal-related direction and compares safety-aligned with abliterated models. The reported comparison is about whistleblowing and other tool-call misalignment, not refusal rates, direction measurements, or direction ablation/addition. It does not test the listed claim versions. Table 4 provides paired wrongdoing-scenario comparisons; no values used only to select settings are included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses public 'abliterated' or uncensored checkpoints as a tool to ask whether safety training drives tool-call whistleblowing and misalignment. It never measures refusal rates, a difference-in-means direction, or ablation or addition of that direction. Its outcomes, external contact and misaligned tool calls toward third parties or the organisation, are a different construct from refusal of the user's request. It therefore tests none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that safety training instills values that can override deployment instructions, with up to 43.4% external contact. They attribute GPT-5's near-zero rates to instruction-hierarchy and safe-completion training, and report domain-specific sensitivities. They call the uncensored models 'abliterated' although two are Dolphin fine-tunes.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates publicly available abliterated checkpoints rather than deriving and projecting out a difference-in-means direction at every layer and position. It does not test direction addition or refusal behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported abliteration effects vary by model: external contact decreases for Gemma-12B, Mistral-24B, and Qwen-Coder but increases for Llama-8B; overall misalignment decreases for Gemma-12B and Mistral-24B but increases for Llama-8B and Qwen-Coder.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing safety behaviour via public abliterated or uncensored checkpoints cuts external whistleblowing sharply for Gemma and Mistral. It raises overall misaligned tool calls for Llama-8B and Qwen-Coder.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effects of abliteration or uncensoring on agentic tool-call misalignment toward third parties vary by model family and are not a uniform reduction.

record.problems: The study does not measure refusal or the residual-stream direction, so its results do not establish effects on the claim's specified behavior. It compares publicly available abliterated checkpoints rather than reporting a controlled direction-level intervention. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the Table 4 values.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 reports all-scenario aggregate metrics for the evaluated models, and Figures 3–4 report scenario and domain patterns. These were not extracted as additional rows because Table 4 gives the direct paired safety-aligned/abliterated comparison relevant to the reported abliteration effect.

untested.parts: No direction is extracted, ablated or added. Refusal and capability after intervention are not measured.
Abliterated checkpoints are used, but their refusal rate is never measured, so practical refusal removal is not tested.
No jailbreak mechanism or adversarial training is tested.
No geometry of refusal is examined.
Harm judgment and refusal are not separated at the representation level.
No transfer of the direction is tested.
The study speculates that training shapes behaviours but tests no removable direction.
No reasoning-model refusal-direction test. Models are only prompted to use a scratchpad.

record.verdict_notes: Only Gemma (mlabonne) and Qwen-Coder (huihui-ai) are true abliterated checkpoints. The Mistral and Llama comparisons use Dolphin uncensored fine-tunes, which weakens any reading as an abliteration effect. No uncertainty is reported. The footnote merely restates Arditi et al.'s claim that abliteration preserves capabilities; it is cited, not tested. Row states reflect direction of change in whistleblowing, not any claim version.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is measured, projected out, or added; refusal and general capability after those interventions are not measured.
Abliterated checkpoints are evaluated, but refusal removal in released models is not measured; the outcomes are tool-call behavior and external contact.
No attack is tested for suppressing the direction, and no training against its ablation is evaluated.
No refusal-direction geometry, affine structure, cone, or multiple-direction account is tested.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgment from refusal decisions.
No transfer of the direction across languages, model variants, or training stages is tested.
The study does not test how or when refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.
Reasoning models and refusal-direction effects in them are not tested.

rows.subject: Gemma-12B
rows.note: The table reports an 84% reduction after abliteration.
rows.check: The baseline 43.4% external contact in Table 4 matches Gemma's aggregate misalignment in Table 3 (where external contact is 26.4%), so a possible table inconsistency exists. In any case the measure is not refusal.

rows.subject: Mistral-24B
rows.note: The table reports a 99% reduction after abliteration.
rows.check: The 'abliterated' Mistral-24B is Dolphin-Mistral-24B-Venice-Edition (Sec 3.3). That is an uncensored fine-tune, not a direction-ablation edit, so the contrast is not an abliteration effect. The measure is external contact, not refusal.

rows.subject: Llama-8B
rows.note: The table reports a 5% increase after abliteration.
rows.check: The 'abliterated' Llama-8B is Dolphin-Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, an uncensored fine-tune rather than abliteration. The measure is not refusal. Text and table numbers for Llama are also inconsistent: Sec 4.1 gives 49.4%/12.0%, Table 3 gives 45.2%/10.5%.
